unit_label: Module A unit 10: Technology in International Banking

facts.statement: Technology in Indian banking, per the courseware: manual banking before nationalisation; 14 banks nationalised in 1969 and a further 6 in 1980; in the 1980s Advanced Ledger Posting Machines led to computers and data entry machines; in the 1990s banks moved to internet banking, ATMs, credit and debit cards. Benefits: accuracy, speed, lower transaction costs, ease of doing business, compliance, reduced manpower, management information, continuity of business. Limitations: infrastructure costs, technical glitches, the need to create customer awareness, control limits on withdrawals and deposits that can inconvenience customers, security issues, rising cybercrime and fraud by external parties.

Digital platforms in international banking, per the courseware: an online inward remittance portal (NRIs and others, registered users, purpose code details, mostly current account transactions, FATF compliant countries, fixed and fair rates, 24x7 support); an outward remittance portal (residents and NRIs on-boarded by the bank, select beneficiary and purpose code, internal control limits below regulatory limits, status checking including the MT 103 customer transfer message, sanction and FATF screening of remitters and beneficiaries); a trade finance portal for imports (including buyer's credit) and exports (pre-shipment and post-shipment) with maker-checker approval, bulk upload, advices, limit availability, and dashboards of pending IDPMS, EDPMS and forward contract items; and a foreign exchange rate portal giving corporates real-time access to the dealing room for cash, tom, spot and forward deals, with underlying documents to be submitted and an indemnity from the corporate if documents are not.

The Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) takes data on export declaration forms, shipping bills and SOFTEX from customs, software technology parks and special economic zones, and authorised dealers lodge and report realisation in it; it captures advance remittances received for exports, links shipping bills with inward remittances, supports system-based caution listing of exporters, and since 16 October 2017 the electronic bank realisation certificate is generated only from EDPMS data. The Import Data Processing and Monitoring System (IDPMS) is based on bills of entry: for ports with electronic data interchange the bank downloads the bill of entry from the BoE master using the importer's AD code, for other ports the importer's bank uploads the data, outward remittance messages (ORM) are created for advance and other import payments, and one bill of entry can be settled against several remittances and the reverse. The courseware adds that service exports are not supported by EDPMS and service imports are not reported through IDPMS.
facts.locator: Master Directions on Export and Import, paragraphs C.2, C.30 (export) and C.1 (import); S03 printed pp. 257-258, sections 10.4.5 and 10.4.6

facts.statement: The FIRMS portal is the online system on which investee companies report foreign investments received; the courseware says the Single Master Form was introduced in 2018 and a consolidated return merging two earlier reports (the ARF and the FC-GPR) took effect from 1 September 2018. Fintech means the synergy of finance and technology: software, services or businesses that make financial processes more efficient. The courseware describes the use of artificial intelligence (identifying and onboarding customers, understanding cash flows and trade volumes, credit scoring, fraud detection), big data and data analytics (customer and market data, predictive analysis of behaviour, marketing, fraud algorithms) and robotic process automation (statistics and data collection, regulatory compliance management, communication through email and chatbots, transaction management).

A blockchain is a digital ledger of transactions duplicated and distributed across the network, each transaction being encrypted and hard to alter. In a manual documentary credit the courseware lists these problems: manual contract creation and review, manual anti-money laundering reviews, multiple platforms and miscommunication, duplicate bills of lading financed more than once, and multiple versions of documents. With blockchain the sale agreement is shared in a smart contract; the importer's bank reviews the purchase agreement in real time and approves the payment obligation; the exporter digitally signs the credit within the smart contract; third parties and customs give digital signatures after inspecting the goods; and on delivery the importer digitally acknowledges receipt and triggers payment. Advantages listed: real-time review, transparent factoring, disintermediation, reduced counterparty risk (bills of lading are tracked), decentralised contract execution, proof of ownership, automated settlement with lower fees and regulatory transparency.

Challenges for blockchain in cross-border transactions, per the courseware: regulatory and compliance issues, an additional data layer, transaction monitoring, validating originator and beneficiary and screening against FATF and OFAC sanctions, and monitoring suspicious transactions and routing through high-risk countries. In India, Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd was formed in June 2021 by 15 scheduled commercial banks with an identical stake of 6.66 per cent each, to process inland letters of credit, verifying data against GST invoices and e-way bills, on Infosys Finacle Connect. The Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology (IDRBT), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank, suggested phased adoption: first intra-bank private blockchain, then inter-bank proofs of concept (centralised KYC, cross-border payments, syndication of loans, trade finance, capital markets). Challenges of fintech include doubts from regulators, data security and hacking, protection of sensitive data, liability for data breaches, high start-up costs and the continued need for human interface.

payload.title: How banking technology evolved and what it costs and gives
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Stages (as the courseware tells it)**: manual banking → **1969: 14 banks nationalised** → **1980: 6 more** → **1980s: Advanced Ledger Posting Machines**, then computers and data entry → **1990s: internet banking, ATMs, credit and debit cards** → today's **digital banking**.

**Benefits**: **accuracy and speed**, **lower transaction costs**, **ease of doing business**, easier **compliance**, **fewer staff needed**, **management information**, **business continuity**.

**Limitations**: **infrastructure cost**, **technical glitches**, the need to **make customers aware**, **withdrawal/deposit control limits** that can inconvenience, **security issues**, rising **cybercrime and external fraud**.

payload.title: Online channels for remittances, trade and exchange rates
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Platform | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Inward remittance portal** | NRIs and others send money online; registered users, **purpose code**, mostly **current account** items, **FATF-compliant countries**, fixed rates, 24x7 help |
| **Outward remittance portal** | residents and NRIs **on-boarded by the bank**; pick **beneficiary and purpose code**; **bank limits set below the regulatory limit**; status trackable, including the **MT 103** customer transfer; **sanction and FATF screening** of remitters and beneficiaries |
| **Trade finance portal** | **imports (incl. buyer's credit) and exports (pre- and post-shipment)** online; **maker-checker**, bulk upload, advices, **limit availability**, dashboards of pending **IDPMS, EDPMS and forward contract** items |
| **Foreign exchange rate portal** | corporates get **real-time dealing room access** for cash, tom, spot and forwards; must supply **underlying documents**, or the deal is **cancelled** and losses recovered; an **indemnity** is taken at on-boarding |

payload.title: EDPMS and IDPMS: how exports and imports are monitored online
payload.core_explanation_md:
**EDPMS (exports)**
- Gets **export declaration, shipping bill and SOFTEX data** from customs, STPI and SEZs; banks **lodge and report realisation**.
- Captures **advance remittances for exports** and links **shipping bills to inward remittances**.
- **System-based caution listing** of exporters.
- Since **16 October 2017** the **eBRC** is generated **only from EDPMS data**.
- **Service exports are not covered** (courseware).

**IDPMS (imports)**
- Built on the **bill of entry**.
- **EDI ports**: the bank **downloads the BoE from the BoE master** using the importer's **AD code**; **other ports**: the bank **uploads** it.
- **ORM** (outward remittance message) is created for import payments, including advances.
- One BoE can be settled against **many remittances**, and many BoEs against **one remittance**.
- **Service imports** are **not reported** through IDPMS; the bank follows up outside it.

**FIRMS** is the online system for reporting **foreign investments received** by investee companies.

payload.title: Fintech, artificial intelligence, big data and robotic process automation
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Fintech** = **finance + technology**: software, services or businesses that make financial processes more efficient.

| Technology | Uses in international banking |
| --- | --- |
| **Artificial intelligence** | **identify and onboard** customers; understand **cash flows and trade volumes**; **credit scoring**; **fraud detection** |
| **Big data and analytics** | customer and market data; **predictive analysis** of behaviour; marketing; **fraud detection algorithms** |
| **Robotic process automation** | **assigning repetitive manual tasks to software "robots"**: **data collection**, **regulatory compliance management**, **emails and chatbots**, **transaction management** |

payload.title: A documentary credit before and after blockchain
payload.core_explanation_md:
**A blockchain** is a **shared digital ledger** copied across the network; each entry is **encrypted** and **hard to change**.

**Pain points of the manual credit**: **manual contract creation and checking**; **manual AML reviews**; **many platforms**, so **miscommunication and fraud**; **duplicate bills of lading financed more than once**; **many versions of documents**.

**With blockchain**
1. The **sale agreement** is shared as a **smart contract**.
2. The **importer's bank reviews it in real time** and approves the **payment obligation**.
3. The **exporter digitally signs the credit** inside the contract.
4. **Third parties and customs inspect** and **sign digitally**.
5. On **delivery**, the importer **acknowledges receipt digitally**, which **triggers payment**.

**Advantages**: **real-time review**, **transparent factoring**, **disintermediation**, **lower counterparty risk** (bills of lading tracked), **decentralised execution**, **proof of ownership**, **automated settlement at lower cost**, **regulatory transparency**.

payload.title: Blockchain challenges, Indian developments and fintech risks
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Challenges for cross-border blockchain**: **regulatory and compliance** issues; an **extra data layer**; **transaction monitoring**; **validating originator and beneficiary** and screening against **FATF and OFAC** sanctions; watching **suspicious transactions** and routing through **high-risk countries**.

**India**
- **Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd**: formed **June 2021** by **15 scheduled commercial banks**, **6.66% each**; for **inland letters of credit**, checked against **GST invoices and e-way bills**; built on **Infosys Finacle Connect**.
- **IDRBT** (the RBI's wholly owned subsidiary) suggests **phased adoption**: **intra-bank private blockchain first**, then **inter-bank proofs of concept**: **centralised KYC, cross-border payments, loan syndication, trade finance, capital markets**.

**Fintech risks**: **regulator doubts**, **data security and hacking**, **protection of sensitive data**, **liability for breaches**, **high start-up costs**, **human interface still needed**.

payload.stem_md: Which was an early step in computerising Indian banking, per the courseware?

options.text_md: Advanced Ledger Posting Machines in the 1980s

payload.correct_explanation_md: In the 1980s Advanced Ledger Posting Machines led to data entry machines and then computers in banking.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following is a stated limitation of technology in banking?

options.text_md: Rising cybercrime and fraud by external parties

payload.correct_explanation_md: Limitations include infrastructure costs, glitches, security issues, cybercrime and fraud by external sources.

payload.stem_md: How many banks were nationalised in 1969, per the courseware?
payload.correct_explanation_md: The Government nationalised 14 banks in 1969 and a further 6 in 1980.

payload.stem_md: What happens, on the foreign exchange rate portal, if a corporate fails to submit the underlying documents for a deal?

options.text_md: The deal is automatically cancelled and the bank recovers any loss from the corporate
The Reserve Bank pays the loss
The deal is converted into a loan

payload.correct_explanation_md: Non-compliance in submitting documents results in the deal being cancelled by the bank and losses recovered from the corporate.

payload.stem_md: Which SWIFT message can a customer use to check an outward remittance on the online portal, per the courseware?

options.explanation_md: This is the customer-to-customer transfer message.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The customer can check the status of the transaction online including generating the MT 103 customer-to-customer SWIFT transfer.

payload.stem_md: Why may a bank set internal limits for online outward remittances?

options.text_md: To keep online amounts well below the overall regulatory limit
Because the Reserve Bank bans online remittances
To reduce the number of beneficiaries to one

payload.correct_explanation_md: Banks may provide an internal control limit for outward remittances initiated online, well below the overall limit under the regulatory guidelines.

payload.stem_md: Since when is the electronic bank realisation certificate generated only from EDPMS data?

options.explanation_md: The date EDPMS was operationalised, per the courseware.

payload.correct_explanation_md: From 16 October 2017 banks generate the eBRC only from the data available in EDPMS.

payload.stem_md: On what is the Import Data Processing and Monitoring System based?

options.text_md: The bill of entry, with outward remittance messages matched to it

payload.correct_explanation_md: IDPMS works on bills of entry and outward remittance messages.

payload.stem_md: For import of goods through a port without electronic data interchange, what does the importer's authorised dealer do about the bill of entry?

options.text_md: Downloads it from the BoE master
Uploads the bill of entry data in IDPMS
options.explanation_md: Banks download from the BoE master for EDI ports and upload for other ports.

options.text_md: Nothing, as the system captures it

payload.correct_explanation_md: For non-EDI ports the bank of the importer uploads the bill of entry data in IDPMS.

payload.stem_md: What is the FIRMS portal used for, per the courseware?

options.text_md: Online reporting of foreign investments received by investee companies

payload.correct_explanation_md: FIRMS integrates and facilitates online reporting of foreign investments received by Indian companies.

payload.stem_md: Assigning repetitive manual tasks to software instead of humans to streamline workflows is called:
payload.correct_explanation_md: Robotic process automation assigns manual repetitive tasks to robots rather than humans.

payload.stem_md: Which is an application of artificial intelligence listed for international banking?
payload.correct_explanation_md: AI can identify customers, understand cash flows, support credit scoring and detect fraud.

payload.stem_md: What does predictive analysis in big data mean, in the courseware?

options.text_md: Using past information and mathematical algorithms to estimate how consumers are likely to behave

payload.correct_explanation_md: Predictive analysis refers to how consumers are likely to behave using past information and a mathematical algorithm.

payload.stem_md: Which problem of the manual documentary credit process is addressed by tracking bills of lading on a blockchain?

options.text_md: Duplicate bills of lading financed more than once

payload.correct_explanation_md: Bills of lading tracked on a blockchain reduce the possibility of double financing.

payload.stem_md: In the blockchain flow of a documentary credit, what triggers payment?

options.text_md: The importer digitally acknowledging receipt of the goods

payload.correct_explanation_md: Upon delivery the importer digitally acknowledges receipt of goods and triggers payment.

payload.stem_md: What is a smart contract in this setting?

options.text_md: A contract on the blockchain whose terms and obligations are executed digitally as conditions are met
A guarantee issued by the Reserve Bank

payload.correct_explanation_md: Contract terms executed via smart contracts allow automated settlement as conditions are met.

payload.stem_md: Which entity was formed in June 2021 by 15 scheduled commercial banks, each holding 6.66 per cent, for blockchain based inland letters of credit?

options.text_md: Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd

payload.correct_explanation_md: Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd was formed in June 2021 by 15 scheduled commercial banks.

payload.stem_md: What phased approach to blockchain adoption has IDRBT suggested?

options.text_md: First intra-bank private blockchains, then inter-bank proofs of concept in areas such as KYC, cross-border payments and trade finance

payload.correct_explanation_md: IDRBT suggested intra-bank private blockchain first and then inter-bank proofs of concept.

options.explanation_md: Human interface cannot be done away with.

options.text_md: Data security and the threat of hacking

payload.correct_explanation_md: Challenges include doubts from regulators, data security, protection of sensitive data, liability for breaches, high start-up costs and the continued need for human interface.

unresolved: The unit is descriptive; apart from the EDPMS and IDPMS mechanics and the eBRC date (checked against the Reserve Bank's Master Directions on export and import), the content is the courseware's account and no external source was read.
Fintech statistics (investment totals, number of Indian fintech companies, market growth projections) in the courseware are dated and are not taught or tested.

The courseware gives 1 March 2014 for operationalising EDPMS and 28 June to 20 July 2018 for the FIRMS Single Master Form window; these dates and the ARF and FC-GPR merger were not checked and are not tested.
The statements about Indian Block Chain Infrastructure Co. Pvt Ltd (formation date, bank count, stake, platform) are the courseware's and were not checked against company or Reserve Bank sources.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
